classes.name: machine
classes.description: The gesture begins with the right hand open, fingers together, palm facing left, resting on the chest. The hand then extends forward and slightly downwards, palm facing down, in a repetitive pushing motion, before returning to the chest. The hand maintains its open, fingers-together shape throughout this rhythmic, back-and-forth movement. An external voice consistently says "nul" during the gesture.

classes.name: loop
classes.description: The "loop" gesture begins with the person standing, slightly hunched forward, head down, and hands resting lightly on the upper thighs with fingers pointing downwards. The movement involves a continuous, gentle rocking of the torso and head: from the initial forward-bent position, the person slowly raises their upper body and head slightly, then gently lowers back into the hunched posture. This creates a repetitive, fluid swaying or "looping" motion of the upper body, with the hands maintaining light contact with the thighs throughout. The gesture is accompanied by a continuous, melodic vocalization, sounding like sustained, often mournful "ah" or "din" sounds, which are integral to the gesture's expressive quality.

classes.name: cest_nul
classes.description: The gesture begins with both hands raised to chest height, elbows bent, palms facing inwards, and thumbs pointing upwards. The hands then rotate inwards, causing both thumbs to point downwards. This "thumbs down" motion is performed simultaneously with both hands and is accompanied by the spoken word "Nulle" or "nul," which means "worthless" or "null" in French. The gesture typically involves two repetitions of this motion and word.

classes.name: drum
classes.description: The gesture begins with both hands clenched into fists, held in front of the body at chest/abdomen height, with elbows bent. The hands then move in a rapid, alternating up-and-down motion, mimicking the striking of two small drums. The movement is primarily wrist and forearm driven, keeping the fists close to the torso. The gesture is characterized by its continuous, rhythmic action, synchronized with distinct, percussive "boom-boom-boom" sounds that emulate drum beats.

classes.name: navigue
classes.description: The individual stands upright with both hands raised to eye level. The index fingers are extended and touch the bridge of the nose or the inner corners of the eyes, while the thumbs are also extended, pointing outwards, and the remaining fingers are curled into a fist. From this initial position, both index fingers perform small, synchronized, circular or rubbing motions around the nose/eye area. This repetitive motion is accompanied by a continuous, high-pitched, hooting "Ooh-ooh-ooh-ooh-ooh" sound, adding a playful or inquisitive auditory element to the gesture. The gaze often follows the finger movements, enhancing the sense of observation or peeking.
